-88.99890,42.27200.name: Advanced Reproductive Center
-88.99890,42.27200.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

19.76312,52.54226.desc: A clinic mapped in OpenStreetMap as offering fertility treatment. OpenStreetMap holds what somebody chose to map, so a country with few points here may be thinly mapped rather than thinly served. That is the reverse of the national registers alongside it, which are close to complete for one country and silent everywhere else. This layer is a cross-check and a source of leads, not a count.

-97.05857,36.11563.name: College of Veterinary Medicine, College of Human Sciences and College of Engineering, Architecture and Technology
-97.05857,36.11563.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Oklahoma State University. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-96.33400,30.62800.name: Sexing Technologies / STgenetics
-96.33400,30.62800.desc: The dominant supplier of sexed semen, allowing breeders to choose the sex of calves. Most dairy calves born are now female, and the male calves that were the by-product are simply not conceived — a welfare problem reduced by removing the animals from existence.

-77.03600,38.90700.name: Farmworker Justice
-77.03600,38.90700.desc: Represents US farmworkers on pesticide exposure, including the herbicides that tolerant engineered crops are grown to be sprayed with. The people applying those chemicals are the group with the highest exposure and the least standing in any approval process, and no biosafety assessment covers them.

-77.03600,38.90700.name: US Donor Conceived Council
-77.03600,38.90700.desc: Advocates for people conceived from donated sperm or eggs, including on access to medical and identity information that clinics promised would stay sealed. Consumer DNA testing broke that promise permanently, and the people affected were not party to the arrangement that made it.

13.40500,52.52000.name: Formo
13.40500,52.52000.desc: Produces dairy proteins by fermentation without a cow, and secured EU novel food clearance for a fungal protein product. Doing this in Germany matters because it is among the most sceptical markets for engineered food in the world, and the route taken was the novel-food one rather than the GMO one.

13.40500,52.52000.name: ENSSER — independent scientific review
13.40500,52.52000.desc: A network of scientists who publish assessments of engineered organisms independently of applicants and regulators. Useful to a person for one specific purpose: a comment in a consultation carries further if it cites published work rather than only local observation, and this is where to look for a scientific counter-argument that has been through review. Its members have also acted as expert witnesses, which is the other place it matters.

6.09300,52.50900.name: Control Union Certifications
6.09300,52.50900.desc: A for-profit certification division of a Dutch inspection group founded in 1920, operating in 70 to 80 countries. It was established in 2002 as a joint venture with Skal, the Dutch foundation that supervises the organic market — so a commercial certifier was set up in partnership with the body that oversees organic operators, which is a different arrangement from a certifier merely being accredited by one. Its parent runs laboratory analysis, pest management, collateral management and vessel performance services alongside the certification arm, for agriculture, energy, maritime and textiles: the same group inspects a cargo, tests it, and certifies the standard it is sold under. Named alongside Ecocert among the certifiers whose organic certification of raw Indian cotton the EU stopped accepting after fraudulent certificates.

6.09300,52.50900.name: Skal Biocontrole
6.09300,52.50900.desc: The body the Dutch state charges with supervising the organic market: it registers operators, inspects them and issues the certification without which nothing may be sold as organic in the Netherlands. It is also the foundation that entered the 2002 joint venture which became Control Union Certifications, the commercial certifier now working in 70 to 80 countries. The supervisor of one national organic market helped found a global certification business, and both appear on this map: one as a regulator, one as a company whose organic certification of raw Indian cotton the EU stopped accepting.
